description: Order-to-cash lifecycle backbone as event-driven microservices (Python 3.14 + FastAPI + Angular/Analog + PostgreSQL + MongoDB + Kafka + NATS). Assessment #9 of the order-to-cash trilogy, and its SECOND REUSE RUN: specs/shared/, the harness, the n8n workflows and the stack-agnostic infra are copied from #8, and #8's review findings are acceptance criteria from the start. progress/history.md must yield an honest three-way #7 vs #8 vs #9 benchmark.

rules.state_machine: pending -> [spec_author] -> spec_ready -> HUMAN APPROVES -> in_progress -> [implementer] -> in_review -> [reviewer] -> done | blocked
rules.shared_spec_is_read_only: a change to specs/shared/ is a spec amendment (SA-n): explicit, human-gated, applied to all three repositories (#7, #8, #9) in the same session — never a silent fork
rules.reused_ids: R<n> ids are #7's. Reusing one asserts the Python realisation satisfies the same requirement #7's and #8's do.
rules.feature_ids: ids 1-43 keep #8's ids and names so the three-way benchmark joins on them; new #9 entries take ids from 200 upwards (200 = public_readme; findings filed during the build from 201)

features.attached_to: projector_read_model (id 24); also affects web_app (id 29) and seed_job (id 12)
acceptance: the phase 12 gate decides, with evidence, between (a) resolving a responder fact's command causationId to the fact that triggered the command — likely an SA-6, applied to #7, #8 and #9, since the RPC requests carry no triggering-fact id today — and (b) keeping R12's semantics and rendering only what a live timeline can show

features.note: Found 2026-10-04 while reviewing the LinkedIn y Web plan (section 3 observation: in the live demo GIFs of #7 and #8 only the last timeline entry shows 'caused by'). Diagnosis: the web is not at fault — both timeline schemas carry causationId and #8's web (apps/web/src/lib/order-detail.ts:101-104) links an entry only when causationId equals another fact's eventId. R12 lets a fact's causationId name the triggering fact OR the command; facts emitted by RPC responders cite the command, which is never in the timeline. #8's own seed documents the divergence: src/Seed/Domain/Sagas/SagaFixtures.cs — 'one link shorter than a live saga's causal chain'. Disposition: decide at the phase 12 gate; not fixed in phase 3.
